This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For Admission On
13.12.2018, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 W.P.(C) No.18734 of 2018 2
 Judgment

This writ petition is filed by the petitioner seeking to quash Ext.P6 stop memo issued by the Secretary of the Malur Grama Panchayat, i.e., the 1st respondent dated 28.05.2018, stating that waste is being discharged from the establishment run by the petitioner causing serious prejudice to the residents of the locality, failing which, appropriate coercive action will be taken by the Panchayat to stop the unit run by the petitioner.

Brief material facts for the disposal of the writ petition are as follows:
2. Petitioner is operating a rice flour manufacturing unit under the name "Malabar Food Products", which, according to the petitioner, is being carried on by securing necessary clearances from all statutory authorities.

It is submitted that, license was being issued by the Panchayat following Ext.P1 licence issued in the year 2006, by paying the licence fee, evident from the receipt produced as Ext.P1(3) dated 22.03.2018.
Ext.P2 is the consent to operate issued by the Pollution Control Board valid up to 31.01.2023, and Ext.P3 is the licence issued by the authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Therefore, according to the petitioner, the unit is being carried on with necessary licences.
3. However, due to personal animosity between the neighbour, i.e., the 3rd respondent and the petitioner, 3rd respondent started to create one or other hindrances to the petitioner.

He has earlier filed a writ petition before this Court,
demanding action by the 1 st respondent to close down the unit, in which, 1st respondent has filed Ext.P4 counter affidavit, stating that, petitioner has not caused any nuisance.

Later, the writ petition was disposed of, as per Ext.P5, directing the 1 st respondent to visit the site after giving due notice and verify if the petitioner is running the unit with statutory compliances and if any violation is observed, to issue notice to the petitioner and abate the same.

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that, without proper application of mind and merely believing the complaints filed by 3rd respondent and others, 1st respondent has issued Ext.P6 stop memo.

Learned counsel also submitted that, during the pendency of this writ petition, a varied consent viz., Ext.P7 was also secured from the Pollution Control Board with respect to the management of waste water flown from the unit.

That apart, it is submitted that, a fresh licence application is submitted before the Secretary of the 1st respondent, seeking issuance of D&O licence, taking into account the varied consent issued by the Pollution Control Board.
However, no action is taken in the application and therefore, petitioner is entitled to continue the operations, deeming that the licence is issued by the Secretary.
5.
A report is submitted by the Environmental Engineer of the Pollution Control Board and has produced the consent given to the petitioner.

Ext.R2(b) communication dated 19.06.2018 is issued by the Board, informing that, petitioner is carrying on washing of rice in the unit and there are no mechanism provided to manage the water arising out of the cleaning process.
Other aspects with respect to the manner in which the unit is run by the petitioner is also pointed out.

6. The 3rd respondent has filed a detailed counter affidavit, explaining the difficulties faced by the residents of the locality, consequent to the waste accumulated in the premises of the unit run by the petitioner, which is causing serious pollution and other problems to the residents of the locality.

Apart from the same, the report submitted by the Pollution Control Board is seriously objected,
stating that the inspection said to have been conducted on 13.06.2018 was without notice to the 1st respondent Panchayat or to the neighbouring residents of the locality, including the 3rd respondent.

That apart, it is pointed out that, the variation of consent was granted without any information to the Panchayat as well as the people residing in the locality, and further that, due to the sound emanated from the machineries of the unit, there is clear air and sound pollution, which has not been taken note of by the Pollution Control Board while granting the consent.
7. I have considered the rival submissions made across the Bar, and perused the pleadings and the documents on record.
8. The prime contention advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner is that, petitioner is having necessary licence from the Panchayat.
However, on a perusal of Ext.P1(3), it is categoric and clear that, petitioner has paid the licence fees only up to the year 2017-18.
The said receipt is dated 22.03.2018.
There is no case for the petitioner that any licence application was submitted by the petitioner 30 days prior to the expiry of the licence for the period 2017-18.
However, petitioner has a case that Ext.P8 notice is issued by the Secretary of the Panchayat on account of the application submitted by the petitioner.

But, it is clear from Ext.P8 that the petitioner has submitted application only on 03.09.2018, in which it is stated that, since a case is pending before the Court, the application submitted by the petitioner cannot be entertained at this stage.

Therefore, the contention advanced by the petitioner that, petitioner is functioning the unit on account of the deemed licence secured by the petitioner, can never be sustained under law, since it is very clear that the application submitted by the petitioner on 03.09.2018 was confronted with Ext.P8 notice dated Erayi Krishnan vs Malur Grama Panchayat on 13 December, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22885362/
3 14.09.2018.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the application submitted by the petitioner can only be treated as an application submitted for consideration of a licence afresh, and it can never be termed as an application for renewal of licence.

Since it is clear from the provisions of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, and the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Issue of Licence to Dangerous and Offensive Trades and Factories) Rules, 1996, that an application is to be submitted for renewal 30 days prior to its expiry.

entities.text: Kerala Panchayat Raj (Issue of Licence to Dangerous and Offensive Trades and Factories) Rules, 1996
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Anyhow, it is clear that, petitioner has secured consent from the Pollution Control Board and later a varied consent also on account of the notice issued by the Pollution Control Board, evident from Ext.R2(b).
9.

Having evaluated the situation, and appreciated the facts on board, in my considered view,
pendency of this writ petition is the sole reason assigned in Ext.P8 order passed by the Secretary for non-consideration of the application submitted by the petitioner on 03.09.2018.
There is no case for either parties that any other litigation is pending by and between the parties.
10. In that view of the matter, it is only appropriate that the writ petition is disposed of with suitable directions.

There will be a direction to the Secretary of the 1st respondent to consider the D&O licence application submitted by the petitioner, taking into account the consent issued by the Pollution Control Board and also by conducting site inspection of the premises in question, after providing opportunity of participation and hearing to the petitioner and the 3rd respondent.

There will be a further direction to the Secretary of the 1st respondent and the Pollution Control Board to ensure that the unit is functioning without causing inconveniences and prejudices to the people residing in the locality, and that no waste is being flown out of the unit so as to interfere with the peaceful and quality life of the people in the locality.

11. While this writ petition was admitted to the files of this Court, an interim order was granted against operation of Ext.P6 stop memo, which is still in force, and the said order will continue to be in force till a decision is taken, as directed above.
The writ petition is disposed of accordingly.
